puzzles.title: The Rusty Padlock
puzzles.question:
A rusty padlock with three number wheels hangs on the first door. A note is tied to it:

"My first digit is the number of sides on a triangle.
My second digit is double my first.
My last digit is the sum of the other two."

What is the 3-digit code?
hints: Work through the clues in order - each one gives you one digit.
A triangle has 3 sides, so the code starts with 3.
3, then 3 x 2 = 6, then 3 + 6 = 9.

puzzles.title: The Ticking Wall
puzzles.question:
Above the second door, something speaks in a riddle:

"I hang on the wall all day and all night.
I never take a single step, yet I keep on running.
I have a face with no eyes, and hands that can hold nothing."

What am I? (one word)
hints: "Running" doesn't have to mean legs - think of something that keeps going.
Its face and hands are made of numbers and pointers.
It tells you the time.
puzzles.explanation: A wall clock hangs on the wall, 'runs' constantly, and has a face and hands.

puzzles.title: The Mysterious Cipher
puzzles.question: Scratched into the third door are two strange words: KLGGHQ GRRU Below them, someone has carved a tiny reminder: A → D Decode the message. The two words are the password.
hints: Every letter has been replaced by another letter the same distance along the alphabet.
A became D, so every letter was shifted 3 places forward. Shift each one 3 places back.
K → H, L → I, G → D ... the first word is HIDDEN.
puzzles.explanation: A Caesar cipher with a shift of 3: K-L-G-G-H-Q → H-I-D-D-E-N, G-R-R-U → D-O-O-R.

puzzles.title: The Locksmith's Missing Word
puzzles.question:
A locksmith's workbench is covered in labels with a word cut out of each one. The same single word fits every gap:

• SKELETON ____
• ____HOLE
• ____BOARD
• ____STONE
• ____NOTE

What is the missing word?
hints: It's a short word, and you're in a locksmith's workshop.
A pianist uses one of the ____BOARD words; an architect needs a ____STONE to hold an arch together.
It's what opens a lock: a ____HOLE is where you put it.
puzzles.explanation: Skeleton key, keyhole, keyboard, keystone, keynote.

puzzles.title: The Three Chests
puzzles.question: Three chests stand before you: one made of OAK, one of IRON and one of GLASS (frosted - you can't see inside). Exactly one chest holds the key to the next door. Each chest has an inscription, and exactly one of the three inscriptions is true: 🪵 OAK: "The key is in this chest." ⚙️ IRON: "The key is not in this chest." 🔮 GLASS: "The key is not in the oak chest." Which chest holds the key?
hints: Try each chest in turn: assume the key is there and count how many inscriptions would be true.
If the key were in the oak chest, both OAK's and IRON's inscriptions would be true - that's too many.
If the key were in the glass chest, IRON's and GLASS's inscriptions would both be true. Only one chest leaves exactly one true inscription.
puzzles.explanation: Key in iron: OAK false, IRON false, GLASS true - exactly one true statement. The other two placements give two true statements.

puzzles.title: The Lantern-Maker's Ledger
puzzles.question: A dusty ledger lies open on the lantern-maker's desk. One line of numbers is circled: 25 · 3 · 29 · 41 · 11 · 37 · 29 In the margin, the lantern-maker wrote: "Each number was once a letter (A = 1, B = 2 ... Z = 26). I doubled every letter, then added one. To read my secret, undo what I did - in reverse." What is the secret word?
hints: Reverse the steps: first subtract 1, then halve.
25 → 24 → 12, which is the letter L. 3 → 2 → 1, which is A.
The numbers become 12 · 1 · 14 · 20 · 5 · 18 · 14. Look at the title of this room.

puzzles.title: The Clockmaker's Escape Hatch
puzzles.question:
The final hatch is sealed by a 4-digit keypad. Five clues are hidden around the room:

📜 On the desk: "All four digits are different, and none of them is zero."
🕯️ On the candle: "The second digit is three times the first."
🗺️ On the map: "The third digit equals the number of rooms you have already escaped."
🪞 On the mirror: "The first and last digits add up to ten."
🔢 On the keypad: "The last digit is a perfect square."

Enter the 4-digit code to escape!
hints: You are in Room 7, so you have already escaped 6 rooms. That's the third digit.
If the second digit is three times the first, the first digit can only be 1, 2 or 3. One of those clashes with the third digit.
First digit 1 gives a last digit of 9 (a perfect square). First digit 3 gives a last digit of 7, which is not.
puzzles.explanation: Third digit = 6. First digit is 1, 2 or 3 (second = 3x first); 2 gives 2-6-6-8 with a repeated 6. Last digit = 10 - first: 9 (square) for 1, 7 (not square) for 3. Code: 1-3-6-9.
